sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas. 2021. The phonetics of Papuan languages in Southern New Guinea: an overview. In Lindsey & Schokkin (eds), Phonetic fieldwork in Southern New Guinea (LD&C SP 24), 5-12. (text held under idii1243)
sources.note: Marori is not among the six languages of the issue; the areal remark 'no tone, no pitch accent or distinctive stress except for Urama' (p.7) is made of the sampled SNG languages, not of Marori specifically.

sources.citation: Wurm, Stefan. 1954. P. Drabbe's study on the languages of South-West New Guinea [review article on P. Drabbe, Talen en Dialecten van Zuid-West Nieuw-Guinea, Micro-Bibliotheca Anthropos 11, 1954]. Anthropos 49: 299-304. (archive.org item anthropos_1954_49, scanned)
sources.note: pp.300-301: Drabbe gave 'slight attention... to stress and intonation - or tone'; p.302: 'Moraorì (the grave accent indicates the position of the stress) which is dealt with on pages 15-26 in 29 paragraphs' - i.e. Drabbe's transcription marks stress with a grave accent (the ethnonym is final-stressed); no word-stress rule for the language is given.

sources.note: Only first-hand grammar of Moraori before Arka; per Wurm 1954 Drabbe marks stress with a grave accent throughout, so pp. 15-26 (opening 'klanken' paragraph) and the stress-marked vocabulary would show where stress falls even if no explicit rule is stated.
